answer: Yes, a meteg is printed. Host letter: mem (the only mem in the word). Vowel: segol. The word reads שְׁלוֹמֶֽךָ.
visible_evidence: The snippet shows only one instance of שלומך, and its lower points are fully visible. I take this to be the occurrence the question means, because the snippet appears cropped to it. Under the shin there is a vertical two-dot sheva. Under the mem there are three dots in a segol pattern, two above and one below. Just left of that segol, still under the mem's lower-left base and before the final kaf, there is a short separate vertical stroke. That stroke is the meteg. It isn't a sheva dot or part of a vowel, and it sits well above the next line of text, so it isn't ink from that line. The final kaf has a qamats inside it. No other vertical stroke appears under the shin, lamed or vav.
